text: In Philadelphia, if you wanted to fight for your own house, you went to a room upstairs in City Hall. Courtroom 478. There was no judge in it.
provenance: It was called **Courtroom 478**, on an upper floor of Philadelphia's City Hall.
But calling it a courtroom is generous. There was no judge in Courtroom 478.

text: The hearings were run by the same prosecutors trying to take your property. No court appointed lawyers. No right to counsel at all.
provenance: The proceedings were run by the very prosecutors trying to take your property. There were no court-appointed lawyers — no right to counsel at all.

text: Owners were handed forms and quietly encouraged not to fight. Miss a date, because work would not let you off or the letter never reached you, and you could lose your home by default.
provenance: Owners were handed forms and, more often than not, encouraged simply not to fight.
And if you missed a date — if you couldn't get off work, if the letter never reached you, if you didn't understand — you could lose your home automatically, by default.

text: This was not a place where justice was weighed. It was a collection department with the seal of the state on the door.
provenance: This was not a place where justice was weighed. It was a collection department with the seal of the state on the door.

text: In an ordinary criminal case the government must prove a person's guilt beyond a reasonable doubt.
provenance: In an ordinary criminal case, the government accuses a *person*, and it has to prove that person's guilt beyond a reasonable doubt.

text: In that room the promise ran backwards. They took first, and left you to prove your way home.
provenance: In Philadelphia, for years, that promise ran backwards. They took first, and left you to prove your way home.

text: It was built to take small amounts from the people least able to fight City Hall.
provenance: It was built to take small amounts, from ordinary people — the people with the least ability to hire a lawyer, take a day off work, and fight City Hall.

text: Courtroom 478 was closed for good in 2018. Between 2002 and 2014 the city had already taken more than twelve hundred homes.
provenance: And Courtroom 478 — the room with no judge — was closed for good.
Between 2002 and 2014, the city of Philadelphia used civil forfeiture to take more than **twelve hundred homes**.
